research_question_and_methods.justification: Matches the score_3 description: the study explicitly aims to identify YFV-specific and conserved flavivirus host interactions, links this work to resurgent YFV public-health concern, and provides detailed AP-MS, CRISPRi, infection, structural, and statistical methods plus public data and code availability. Figure 3 further documents functional validation of a prioritized interaction using knockdown, co-IP, and replicon assays.
research_question_and_methods.quote: Here, we map YFV interactomes in human and mosquito cells to identify interactions common among divergent flaviviruses or unique to YFV.

results_and_conclusion.justification: Matches the score_3 description: findings are supported by orthogonal methods, including AP-MS, CRISPRi knockdown, plaque assays, endogenous co-immunoprecipitation with RNase treatment, and replicon assays (Figure 3). The conclusions are appropriately tied to these data, and the paper explicitly discusses methodological and biological limitations on page 20.
results_and_conclusion.quote: Together, our data support a model in which RBBP6 acts as a YFV restriction factor by inhibiting YFV genome replication through a complex RNA-mediated interaction with NS5.

references.justification: The reference list provides broad domain coverage, including foundational flavivirus biology, AP-MS and interaction-scoring methods, CRISPR screens, evolutionary analyses, and recent YFV surveillance. It predominantly cites peer-reviewed, high-quality journals such as Nature, Cell, Science, PNAS, and eLife, while using a limited number of recent preprints and public-health reports where directly relevant.
references.quote: Comparative Flavivirus-Host Protein Interaction Mapping Reveals Mechanisms of Dengue and Zika Virus Pathogenesis.
